description: Verify that DUT re-picks its Link-Local address after a probing-window ARP Request conflict (RFC 3927 §2.2.1, MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 3927 §2.2.1 mandates that during the probing phase, if any host claims the tentative address (via ARP Request, Reply or another Probe), the prober MUST abandon it and pick a fresh one. This case injects a conflicting ARP Request immediately after DUT's first Probe and asserts the next Probe targets a different LL.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: OpStartLLAutoconf (kicks the Link-Local state machine)

2. DUT → wire: first ARP Probe with target_proto_ip = tentative_LL
   • SCXML transitions to await_repick on this Probe; the entry observer fires immediately and reads c.first_probe_target_proto_ip so the conflict frame claims exactly the DUT's tentative LL

3. Tester → DUT: ARP Request, sender_proto_ip = tentative_LL (the address DUT just probed)

4. Observation:
   • DUT → wire: a fresh ARP Probe with target_proto_ip ≠ tentative_LL   ← key check

[Pass condition]
First DUT Probe AND a follow-up Probe targeting a different LL after the conflict.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_initial_probe — DUT did not emit any initial ARP Probe within the deadline
• Fail_no_repick — DUT did not re-probe with a different LL after the conflict ARP Request

verdicts.Pass: DUT re-picked its LL after the conflict ARP Request — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_initial_probe: DUT did not emit any initial ARP Probe within the deadline
verdicts.Fail_no_repick: DUT did not re-probe with a different LL after the conflict ARP
